- Model consistently underestimates prices during sharp upward spikes (e.g., 48.12, 49.30, 51.55) and overestimates during sharp downward moves.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, especially in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- After a spike, model often overshoots the true value in the following days, suggesting failure to capture mean reversion or volatility decay.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day forecast, particularly after mid-2023.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture abrupt volatility or sudden reversals (e.g., 34.33, 33.70, 32.56 in Example 5).
- Model underreacts to recent high volatility or low prices in the history window, leading to conservative forecasts.
